title: AI-guided HuJ3 mutation improves HIV-1 gp120 binding and neutralization in assays
summary: The IsAb2.0 workflow, combining AlphaFold-Multimer complex modeling with FlexddG mutation scoring, proposed five substitutions to improve the binding of humanized J3 nanobody HuJ3 to HIV-1 gp120. Of these, E44R experimentally improved binding (ELISA EC50 1.696 nM) and neutralization relative to HuJ3; the other proposed substitutions did not consistently improve binding, and T99R failed to express. The gain did not restore neutralization to the parental llama J3 level.
ai_technology: IsAb2.0 antibody-design protocol integrating AlphaFold-Multimer 2.3/3.0, SnugDock, alanine scanning and FlexddG
organization: University of Pittsburgh School of Pharmacy; University of Pittsburgh Center for Antibody Therapeutics; University of Pittsburgh Center for AIDS Research

evidence.tested: Of these, E44R experimentally improved binding (ELISA EC50 1.696 nM) and neutralization relative to HuJ3; the other proposed substitutions did not consistently improve binding, and T99R failed to express.
evidence.unknown: This is a single, previously known J3 nanobody humanization/optimization case, not de novo antibody discovery, animal efficacy or clinical evidence. Only one of five proposed mutants improved binding; several predictions failed and the authors note limitations in prediction accuracy and manual steps. E44R remained less potent than parental J3.
evidence.ai_role: The protocol modeled the HuJ3–gp120 complex, nominated interface hotspots and computationally ranked five single-residue mutations. Researchers synthesized/tested variants in binding and HIV-1 neutralization assays; the measured E44R improvement is the experimental outcome, while most predictions did not improve performance.
